prompt_en: Refine the stage tableau in Image 2, using Image 1 for the woman's visible portrait appearance and preserving the established six-role layout. A staged editorial photograph of a complex religious and mythic test scene in a black-box theater. At center, a fictional adult woman, explicitly a 28-year-old performer portraying a deceased soul, stands beside an open upright funerary coffin. The supplied portrait guides only the visible facial proportions, rounded dark eyes, soft lips, and dark chin-length bob with wispy fringe. Her ivory satin stage dress and still, alert bearing give her a quietly magnetic presence. She deliberately holds her place before the balance. One waist-high brass Egyptian judgment balance stands before her. Its left pan holds her ceramic red anatomical-heart prop, its right pan holds one upright white feather of Maat; the beam is level. A jackal-headed adult Anubis performer touches the balance's central plumb line. An ibis-headed adult Thoth performer writes this same balanced outcome: the reed pen's visible nib touches the open papyrus face beneath its heart-and-feather balance diagram and leaves a fresh black ink stroke. A bright blue thumbnail-sized cartouche plate on the heart's visible front surface matches the blue medallions on woman and coffin. Behind her the admission arch is open and warmly lit, showing the favorable judgment's route toward the upper realm. Across the foreground, three distinct adult Moirai performers handle one thick crimson life-thread: Clotho draws loose crimson flax fibers between her two visible fingers into a newly twisted strand on a slender drop spindle, Lachesis stretches the next segment along a marked measuring rod, and Atropos's silver shears close at a clearly visible finger-width gap between two freshly severed tips of that same strand. The connected course from spindle to rod to the cutting point is fully visible. Beyond the single cut gap, the downstream crimson strand rises diagonally through clear space to fasten visibly to the woman's blue chest medallion. A single sculptural world-axis tree fills the rear stage, its continuous trunk rising from a visible dark subterranean root chamber through an inhabited earth platform into a celestial crown under a luminous star canopy. The same tree visibly connects all three vertically separated realms. The slightly raised frontal camera shows all six role owners, every thread-hand contact, both scale pans, tree roots, and crown together.
